EditorPrefs variations: 1. Simple Boolean: GetBool/SetBool with toggle callbacks; 2. String URL/Path: GetString/SetString with FocusOut; 3. Integer Port: GetInt/SetInt with KeyDown validation; 4. Key Deletion: DeleteKey() for clearing overrides; 5. Scope-Aware: Conditional logic based on transport scope

One-time read sync: 1. CreateGUI/Constructor called -> 2. CacheUIElements queries elements -> 3. InitializeUI reads EditorPrefs once -> 4. SetValueWithoutNotify or .value = ... to populate UI -> 5. No automatic refresh if EditorPrefs change externally -> 6. Manual refresh requires RefreshUI() call
Pattern in 5 components: Phase 1: CacheUIElements() - Root.Q<T>() queries -> Phase 2: InitializeUI() - EditorPrefs reads + defaults -> Phase 3: RegisterCallbacks() - Event handler setup

Write-through sync: 1. User modifies UI element (toggle, field, dropdown) -> 2. Callback fires immediately -> 3. EditorPrefs.Set* called in callback -> 4. No batching or delayed persistence -> 5. Each change writes immediately to EditorPrefs
EditorPrefsWindow caches 2 base UI elements: ScrollView + Container
Callback pattern: Each item gets: saveButton.clicked += () => SavePref(item, value, type)

Type detection flow: 1. Check knownPrefTypes dictionary for known keys; 2. For unknown keys: EditorPrefs.GetString() first; 3. Try int.TryParse(); 4. Try float.TryParse(); 5. Try bool.TryParse(); 6. Default to String if all fail

Event signaling: 1. Component declares: public event Action OnSomethingHappened; -> 2. Raises event: OnSomethingHappened?.Invoke(); -> 3. Other component subscribes: connection.OnSomethingHappened += HandleIt; -> 4. Flow: ConnectionSection -> AdvancedSection or ClientConfigSection -> 5. Used for: transport changes, config updates, manual refresh requests

Dynamic class list pattern: element.AddToClassList("valid"); element.RemoveFromClassList("invalid"); Used for path validation, status indicators, etc.
Advanced section uses 6 EditorPrefs keys
Toggle callback pattern: toggle.RegisterValueChangedCallback(evt => {...}); EditorPrefs.SetBool(Key, evt.newValue); Optional: invoke domain events or refresh UI
McpClientConfigSection caches 22 UI elements

Cascading update flow: 1. dropdown.RegisterValueChangedCallback(evt => {...}); 2. Load config for selected client; 3. Update dependent fields (URL, status, etc.); 4. Show/hide sections based on selection; 5. Invoke update events for other components
Dropdown initialization: dropdown.choices = configuratorList; dropdown.index set from current selection; Choices populated from service/registry
DisplayStyle pattern: element.style.display = DisplayStyle.None; element.style.display = DisplayStyle.Flex; Used for showing/hiding config fields based on dropdown selection
McpConnectionSection caches 24 UI elements. Examples: transportDropdown, httpUrlField, unityPortField, statusIndicator, connectionStatusLabel, connectionToggleButton
McpConnectionSection events: OnManualConfigUpdateRequested, OnTransportChanged
McpConnectionSection reads EditorPrefs: MCPForUnity.UseHttpTransport, MCPForUnity.HttpTransportScope, MCPForUnity.UnitySocketPort

Transport callback flow: 1. Get previous and new transport values; 2. Persist UseHttpTransport to EditorPrefs; 3. Persist HttpTransportScope if HTTP; 4. Clear resume flags (ResumeStdioAfterReload in EditorPrefs, HTTP resume key in SessionState); 5. Update UI visibility; 6. Invoke OnManualConfigUpdateRequested event; 7. Invoke OnTransportChanged event; 8. Stop opposing transport if switching HTTP<->Stdio
FocusOut pattern: httpUrlField.RegisterCallback<FocusOutEvent>(_ => PersistHttpUrlFromField()); Avoids fighting user during typing; Normalizes URL on commit
KeyDown pattern: field.RegisterCallback<KeyDownEvent>(evt => {...}); if (evt.keyCode == KeyCode.Return || evt.keyCode == KeyCode.KeypadEnter); PersistValue(); evt.StopPropagation();
MCPSetupWindow caches 22 UI elements including: pythonIndicator, pythonVersion, pythonDetails, uvIndicator, uvVersion...
Class list modification: indicator.RemoveFromClassList("invalid"); indicator.AddToClassList("valid"); Or vice versa for unavailable dependencies
